rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the most important first step is to establish a simple, well-understood baseline. config_001 (RNA-only, single profile, PCA-n2000) is the most minimal configuration in the search space: no learned encoder, no aggregation, no fusion. It provides a clean reference for RNA-only performance and a floor against which all more complex choices (learned encoders, multiprofile aggregation, multimodal fusion) must be compared. Starting here reduces uncertainty about the baseline signal quality and ensures that any gains observed in later experiments can be attributed to specific design choices rather than confounded by multiple simultaneous changes. It is the natural anchor point for a sequential search with a 10-experiment budget.

Evidence: The only completed experiment (config_001, rna_only/singleprofile/pca_n2000) achieved a low validation accuracy of ~48.5%, leaving substantial uncertainty about whether the RNA modality alone is sufficient or whether the image modality carries complementary signal. Question: This experiment tests whether an image-only model (resnet50, singleprofile) can achieve comparable or better accuracy, directly isolating the modality question while holding profile setting (singleprofile) and model complexity constant relative to config_001. Why: With 8 experiments remaining, resolving whether image features are informative is the highest-impact early decision—if image-only performs well, the multimodal space (configs 016–051) becomes a promising exploitation target; if it performs poorly, we can focus remaining budget on RNA encoder and profile improvements. This is a clean, single-variable comparison that maximally reduces uncertainty about the most fundamental design axis.

Evidence: RNA-only with PCA n2000 (config_001) achieves 48.5% accuracy, while image-only ResNet50 (config_010) is very weak at 20.8%, indicating RNA is the dominant signal. The key uncertainty is whether the linear PCA representation is limiting performance or whether a learned nonlinear encoder (scvi_n200) could capture richer structure. This experiment (config_004: RNA-only, single profile, scvi_n200) isolates the encoder effect by changing only the RNA encoder relative to config_001, keeping profile setting and model setting identical. If scvi_n200 significantly outperforms PCA n2000, it justifies prioritizing scvi-based multiprofile and multimodal configs in the remaining budget; if it does not, PCA-based configs remain competitive and we can focus on profile/aggregation or fusion questions. With 7 experiments left, resolving the representation question early maximizes the value of subsequent multiprofile and multimodal tests.

Evidence: scvi_n200 (0.520 acc) outperforms pca_n2000 (0.485 acc) in RNA-only singleprofile, and image-only is very weak (0.208 acc), making RNA the dominant signal. Uncertainty: we have not yet tested whether multiprofile aggregation adds value over singleprofile for the best encoder. This experiment (config_005: rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) isolates the profile-setting effect by changing only profile from single to multi while holding the encoder (scvi_n200) and model setting (rna_only) fixed, using the simpler avgpool aggregation. It is the best next step because it directly extends our current best result with a single-variable change, reducing uncertainty about whether multiprofile is worth pursuing before committing remaining budget to more complex multimodal or transformer-aggregation variants.

The strongest result so far is config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) at 0.650 acc, a large jump over singleprofile (0.520). The key open question is whether transformer aggregation can further improve over avgpool for multiprofile scvi_n200. Config_006 is a clean single-variable comparison (avgpool → transformer) that directly extends the best configuration. Resolving this is critical before spending remaining budget on multimodal fusion: if transformer wins, it sets a stronger base for downstream multimodal experiments; if avgpool holds, we confirm the aggregation choice and can pivot to testing scgpt or multimodal extensions. With 5 experiments left, isolating the best aggregation for the dominant modality is the highest-value uncertainty reduction.

Evidence: The best result so far is config_006 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, transformer) at 0.653 acc. We've established that (a) multiprofile is a major gain over singleprofile (+0.13), (b) scvi_n200 beats pca_n2000, and (c) transformer vs avgpool aggregation makes negligible difference (~0.003). Uncertainty: We have not tested whether scgpt, a fundamentally different RNA representation (autoregressive generative model vs VAE), could outperform scvi_n200 in the multiprofile setting. This experiment isolates the RNA encoder effect while holding the proven multiprofile + transformer pipeline constant. Rationale: With 4 experiments remaining, establishing the best RNA-only baseline is critical before investing in multimodal fusion (which adds complexity and the image modality alone was very weak at 0.21). If scgpt matches or beats scvi_n200, it opens a new encoder direction; if not, we confirm scvi_n200 as optimal and can focus remaining budget on testing whether multimodal fusion adds value on top of the best RNA-only config.

The current best is config_006 (RNA-only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, transformer) at 0.653. The dominant finding is that multiprofile + scvi_n200 drives most of the gain, while image-only resnet50 is very weak (0.21), suggesting the image modality may carry little signal. The key remaining question is whether a stronger image encoder (ViT-L) combined with the proven best RNA setup (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer) can push past 0.653 via fusion. Config_038 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) is the most direct test: it pairs the strongest RNA configuration with the strongest available image encoder in a standard concat fusion. If it exceeds 0.653, it identifies a new best and leaves 2 experiments to refine fusion (e.g., weighted). If it does not, it confirms the image modality is not contributing useful signal, and we can confidently stop at 0.653 with the remaining budget. This is the highest-information single experiment given only 3 slots remain.

The current best is config_038 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) at 0.721 accuracy. The only untested variable within this exact configuration family is the fusion strategy: weighted vs. concat. Config_039 changes only the fusion from concat to weighted, making it a clean single-variable comparison that directly tests whether learned weighting of the two modalities can outperform simple concatenation. This is the highest-value exploitation step: it isolates one design choice on the most promising configuration, and if weighted fusion helps, it could push accuracy above 0.721. With only 2 experiments remaining after this, a targeted test of the current best's fusion mechanism is more informative than exploring a new encoder or aggregation that showed negligible differences in the RNA-only setting.

Evidence: The current best is config_039 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile + transformer + weighted, acc=0.725), with config_038 (same but concat) at 0.721. In RNA-only, transformer (0.653) marginally beat avgpool (0.650), suggesting aggregation choice has a small effect. Question: Does avgpool aggregation with weighted fusion in the multimodal setting perform comparably to or better than transformer, potentially by reducing overfitting or interaction complexity? This is the closest untested variant to the current best (only aggregation changes from transformer→avgpool), isolating that single factor. With only 1 experiment remaining, this is the highest-expected-value test: it either confirms 0.725 as the plateau or reveals a small improvement, while avoiding high-variance jumps (e.g., switching to scgpt or resnet50) that are strongly disfavored by prior evidence.

The current best is config_039 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250. The evidence strongly supports scvi_n200 as the best RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l as the best image encoder, multiprofile over single, transformer aggregation over avgpool, and weighted over concat fusion. Config_036 (same backbone but avgpool + concat) is the only remaining untested cell in the 2×2 aggregation×fusion grid for this best architecture. While it is unlikely to surpass 0.7250, it completes the design-space comparison, confirming that both transformer aggregation and weighted fusion contribute to the peak performance. As the final experiment with no budget remaining, this is the most informative exploitation choice: it validates the ranking of aggregation and fusion effects within the best model family rather than chasing a low-probability alternative encoder that the RNA-only and image-only evidence already disfavors.
